claude-opus-5-5.note: Anthropic list; caching OFF on this account, so a ceiling

convergence.meaning: Two claims are the same structure when they name the same side and their fitted lines differ by <= 0.5 ATR in mean absolute separation across the window.
convergence.effect: converged windows are excluded from the fabrication count and listed separately

decisionRule: Higher AUC separating A from B wins. If the intervals overlap, fit quality on C decides. If that overlaps too, cost per call. A tie builds on Grok. Written before any comparison existed - Claude had produced zero results at the time, so there was no outcome to favour. The first rule (fewest fabrications on B) was retired for NON-DISCRIMINATION, measured: 0 structures on both groups with the refusal sentence, 3 on both without it.
caveats: Claude cost is an UPPER BOUND: prompt caching is off on the account.
Groups were assigned by scripts/bakeoff/classify.mjs against a shuffled-returns null, which is an easier null than real price - so z is inflated and the C band should not be over-read.
Engines are scored by the same geometry that chose the fixtures; a structure our code cannot see lands in B. The convergence rule is the only guard against that.

perWindow.note: PRIMARY. Highest confidence per window-run. 0.5 is chance; below 0.5 means the engine was more confident about noise than about structure.

perClaim.note: SECONDARY. Pools every candidate, so n is larger and the values are CORRELATED - three candidates from one reply are not three independent opinions. No interval is given, because a bootstrap over correlated draws would understate the uncertainty.
